text:
Chief Executive Officer: This quarter we shipped our third system to a national laboratory, and we signed two new paid cloud access contracts with industrial customers. Revenue from system sales and cloud access grew 40% from a year ago.

Chief Executive Officer: Our customers are still in the evaluation phase. We believe they will run production workloads where our systems beat classical computers in 3 to 5 years, and our roadmap is built around that window.

Chief Financial Officer: Demand for our post-quantum encryption gateway was strong. Government buyers are preparing because quantum computers could break RSA within 5 years, and they want to replace vulnerable keys before that happens.

Analyst: Is the new gateway priced at a premium?

Chief Financial Officer: Yes, about 20% above the previous generation.

Chief Executive Officer: We continue to see quantum computing as a long-term opportunity. We fund research partnerships with three universities, and our engineers built prototype cryogenic control chips that our partners are testing in their laboratories.

Chief Executive Officer: None of this is material to revenue, and we do not expect it to be for some time.

Analyst: Some people say useful quantum computers are 15 to 30 years away. Do you agree with that view?

Chief Executive Officer: We don't give timelines. Our team is focused on error-correction research in our own laboratory, and we will report results when we have them.

Chief Executive Officer: A national parcel carrier now runs our quantum optimization service in its daily production planning. Routing that took the carrier's classical solver 9 hours now takes 4 minutes, and the carrier has extended the contract for three years.

Chief Scientific Officer: Three pharmaceutical partners are running proofs of concept on a cloud quantum computing service at no charge, to test whether it can screen molecules faster than our current methods. We expect the first paid contract next year.

Chief Technology Officer: This quarter our engineers completed a 100-qubit chip with improved gate fidelity. We plan to deliver a 1,000-qubit processor by 2027, which is the next step on our hardware roadmap.

Chief Executive Officer: Customers access our quantum computers today through paid research agreements. We expect quantum advantage for our customers' chemistry simulations, meaning better results than classical methods in their own product development, by 2030.

Chief Executive Officer: Data center revenue reached a record. Several financial customers now use quantum-inspired algorithms running on our GPUs for portfolio optimization, which shows the strength of our accelerated computing platform.
Chief Executive Officer: Practical quantum computing at scale is still decades away, in my view. Until then our business is classical test equipment, and that is where we invest.

Chief Executive Officer: Today our revenue comes from system sales to research centers and from paid cloud access. Within the next 2 to 3 years, we expect the first commercial applications where quantum computers beat classical machines for paying customers.

Chief Financial Officer: I am not convinced quantum computers will ever beat classical machines for routing problems, so we are not investing there. Our research spending goes to classical optimization.
